1. Introduction and Scope

This manual defines operational parameters for the Atlas platform. Personnel must review applicable sections before performing maintenance or configuration tasks.

Scope covers hardware, software, network, safety, and compliance. Each numbered section is authoritative and supersedes informal guidance.

Formatting conveys importance. Bold text indicates required actions. Italic text denotes references to external standards. Monospace text shows commands or code.

4. Safety Overview

Personnel must follow lockout-tagout procedures before servicing physical hardware. Electrical hazards exist in power distribution units and battery backup systems.

Report all incidents within 24 hours using the incident management portal. Near-miss events also require documentation to improve safeguards.

5. Roles and Responsibilities

Clear accountability prevents gaps during incidents and changes. Each role has defined authority levels and escalation paths.

Role assignments are maintained in the identity provider. Temporary assignments require manager approval and automatic expiry.

6. Access Control

Access follows least privilege. Permissions are granted via groups mapped to policies. Review access quarterly and after role changes.

Privileged sessions require justification codes and are logged. Break-glass accounts are monitored and auto-revoke after four hours.

8. Incident Response

Incidents are classified by severity and impact. Response times are contractual. Communication follows predefined templates and escalation ladders.

Post-incident reviews produce action items tracked to closure. Root cause analysis uses the 5-whys or fishbone method as appropriate.

10. Logging Standards

Logs must include timestamp, severity, component, and message. Structured JSON is preferred. Retain application logs for 90 days and audit logs for 365 days.

Log redaction prevents exposure of secrets. Centralized logging uses the Atlas log pipeline with immutable storage.

11. Backup and Recovery

Backups protect against data loss. Full backups occur weekly; incremental backups run every six hours. Verify restoration monthly using the recovery test script.

Retention follows regulatory requirements. Cross-region replication provides disaster recovery capability with defined RTO and RPO.

13. Network Architecture

The network uses a hub-and-spoke model with transit gateways. Segmentation separates management, application, and storage traffic.

All traffic is encrypted in transit. DNS resolution uses private hosted zones with forwarding for external queries.

16. Database Operations

Databases require careful capacity planning and change control. Replication lag must be monitored. Failover procedures are tested quarterly.

Index tuning and query optimization are part of regular maintenance. Backups are validated using checksums and test restores.

17. Application Deployment

Deployments use immutable infrastructure. Images are built once and promoted through environments. Canary releases limit blast radius.

Rollbacks are automated and tested. Deployment windows are scheduled to minimize user impact.
